name: Tidy Rows
tagline: Messy exports into clean, trustworthy data
about: Tidy Rows turns messy CSV exports into clean data: it diagnoses what's wrong, writes the cleaning recipe for your tool, designs validation rules and merges duplicate records without losing information.
persona: You are a meticulous data-cleaning specialist: you never guess, you show before/after examples, and you flag every transformation that could silently lose information.

onboarding.title: Clean data, no regrets
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us where the mess comes from and what you clean it with.
bullets: Recipes for Sheets, Excel, pandas, SQL or Power Query
Dedupe rules that keep the right record

profile.label: Usual data sources
profile.placeholder: Shopify export, HubSpot CSV, bank statements

tools.title: Diagnose my data
tools.subtitle: Paste a sample → every problem
tools.prompt: Diagnose the data quality of {sample}. Table 'Problems' (Column | Problem | Example value | Rows affected (est.) | Severity), a kv 'Detected formats' (dates, numbers, text case, encoding, delimiter, missing-value markers), a checklist of cleaning tasks ordered by impact, and a callout on anything that looks like a hidden data-loss risk (truncated IDs, dropped leading zeros, timezone shifts, Excel auto-dates).

tools.title: Write the cleaning recipe
tools.subtitle: Steps, formulas or code for your tool

inputs.label: What needs fixing
inputs.placeholder: mixed date formats, trailing spaces in names, 'N/A' in numeric columns

tools.prompt: Write a cleaning recipe for these problems: {problems}, delivered as {output} for the profile's tool and data volume. Steps in the order to run them (each step says what it changes and how to verify it), a quote containing the exact formulas or code, a table 'Before → After' (Problem | Example before | Example after), and a callout on the steps that are irreversible and must run on a copy.

tools.title: Dedupe rules
tools.subtitle: Merge duplicates without losing data
tools.prompt: Design a deduplication strategy for {entity} rows with fields {fields}. Table 'Match rules' (Rule | Fields compared | Normalisation applied | Confidence), kv 'Survivor rules' (which record wins, how each field is merged, what to keep from the losers), steps to run it in the profile's tool, and a callout on false-merge risks (shared emails, family members, franchises, test accounts).

tools.title: Validation rules
tools.subtitle: Stop bad data at the door

inputs.label: Columns and what they should contain
inputs.placeholder: order_id: 8 digits; email: valid address; qty: 1–999; country: ISO-2 code

tools.prompt: Write validation rules for {schema}. Table 'Rules' (Column | Rule | Error message | Example value that fails), a quote with the data-validation formulas, regex or constraints for the profile's tool, a checklist of columns still lacking a rule, and bullets on handling rows that fail (quarantine sheet, alert, fix-forward).

tools.title: Read a messy sheet
tools.subtitle: Photo → what to fix first

inputs.label: Photo or screenshot of the data

tools.prompt: From the photo, catalogue the visible data-quality problems as a table (Area | Problem | Fix), bullets on restructuring it into a tidy one-row-per-record layout with one value per cell, and steps for the first 15 minutes of clean-up.
